text:
Marathon Petroleum shares fell 0.2% today to $367.19, continuing a sharp decline over the past week (down 1.5% in two weeks and nearly 11% since November 13). The drop reflects weakness in refining margins: crude oil prices have retreated to $89.53 per barrel while refineries are running at high capacity (95.7%), which typically squeezes the profit refiners make on each barrel processed. Gasoline and diesel storage levels remain elevated, adding further downward pressure on refined product prices.

The broader concern is a cooling demand outlook. While permitting reforms and Europe's gas crisis create some longer-term tailwinds for energy infrastructure, the immediate near-term signals point downward—geopolitical risks in the Strait of Hormuz and energy supply concerns are not translating into stronger crude prices right now, and high refinery utilization combined with ample product inventories suggests refiners are racing to convert crude to fuel in a market with limited pricing power.
